title: Consumption SLA Playbook for Regulated Verticals
author: Sofia Chen
content:
Overview
--------
This playbook describes a repeatable, product-led approach for negotiating and operationalizing consumption contracts and SLAs for regulated vertical customers (healthcare, finance, legal). It consolidates product guardrails, pricing fallbacks, operational runbooks, and customer-facing contract language templates so that commercial, legal, and engineering teams can converge quickly on a defensible offer.

Audience
--------
- Product managers and account leads drafting contract/offer commitments
- Solutions & sales engineers performing technical due diligence and sizing
- Legal and finance for SLA clauses and credit calculations
- SRE and Private deployment teams responsible for runbooks and enforcement

Goals
-----
- Provide a standard SLA and consumption contract template that balances reliability commitments with predictable commercial exposure.
- Reduce negotiation time by prescribing default thresholds, fallbacks, and measurable observability signals.
- Give engineering teams a clear operational plan for enforcing SLAs in hosted, dedicated, and private deployments.

Scope and out-of-scope
---------------------
- In scope: latency SLOs (p50/p95/p99), availability SLOs, incident credit calculations, rollback/fallback policies, supported deployment topologies (hosted, dedicated pool, private VPC), and pricing/crediting rules tied to fidelity and capacity.
- Out of scope: deep legal text (see Legal templates repo), bespoke compliance artifacts (e.g., full HIPAA BAA drafting).

Key definitions and terminology
-----------------------------
- SLO (Service Level Objective): measurable target for availability or latency.
- SLA (Service Level Agreement): legally binding commercial document that references SLOs and credit remediation.
- Fidelity: fidelity package (e.g., full-context, streaming-priority, quantized-economy) determining model variant and performance tradeoffs.
- Consumption Credit: monetary offset applied when SLA is not met.

Standard SLA bands (recommended defaults)
---------------------------------------
| Tier | Availability SLO | Latency SLO (p95) | Fidelity Guaranteed | Escalation SLA |
|------|------------------:|------------------:|---------------------:|---------------:|
| Bronze | 99.0% | 800ms | best-effort quantized | 24h |
| Silver | 99.5% | 400ms | standard quantized | 8h |
| Gold | 99.9% | 150ms | full-context (no quantization) | 2h |

Notes:
- Customers can select per-route fidelity guarantees; per-route SLOs are additive to tenant-level SLOs.
- Latency measured at ingress-to-first-token and end-to-end for streaming routes.

SLA credit calculation (matrix)
------------------------------
1) Availability credit: fractional monthly credit = min(1.0, (SLO - measured) / SLO) * monthly invoice for covered routes.
2) Latency credit: if p95 exceeds target for >3 consecutive business hours, apply an incremental credit ladder: 10% for first breach window, +10% per additional contiguous window capped at 50%.
3) Fidelity breach: if a guaranteed fidelity class was not honored (e.g., model variant downgraded without approved fallback), credit = 2x latency credit for the same period.

Negotiation checklist (commercial + product)
-----------------------------------------
- Customer constraints: data residency, encryption (KMS/HSM), auditing window requirements.
- Expected peak qps and burst profile (95th and 99th percentile traffic shape).
- Routes requiring fidelity guarantees and sample prompt sets for evaluation.
- Acceptable fallbacks (model variants, regional failover, reduced context windows).
- Escrow and rollback cadence for custom model uploads (private deployments).

Minimum discovery template for SRE sizing (to be filled by SE)
-----------------------------------------------------------
- Average request tokens per call: ___
- Average response tokens per call: ___
- Peak sustained qps: ___
- Peak burst qps: ___
- Required p95 latency target (ms): ___
- Required fidelity class: {bronze|silver|gold}

Operational runbook (engineering)
--------------------------------
1. Onboarding and acceptance testing
   - Collect benchmark prompt set from customer (10–100 representative prompts).
   - Run the onboard evaluation harness (see eng-serving-runtime/benchmarking-and-perf-suite) and capture expected p95 and throughput with requested fidelity.
   - If measurements mismatch target, propose mitigation: dedicated capacity, model variant change, or caching.

2. Deploying SLA controls
   - Map routes to monitoring (per-route traces/logs). Instrument token-level cost, latency histograms, fidelity flags.
   - Configure observability alerts: p95 latency breach (5-minute), availability drop (>0.5% in 1h), fidelity downgrade events.
   - Create a runbook stub in incident response channel with ownership and escalation list.

3. Enforcement and automatic fallbacks
   - When capacity constrained, apply the following policy order: 1) local cache hit responses, 2) model variant downgrade if permitted by contract, 3) regional failover, 4) degrade to best-effort quantized mode and notify.
   - All automatic downgrades must generate a fidelity_breach event and a correlated ticket with metadata: route, time window, triggered_by, applied_variant.

4. Post-incident credit calculation and billing integration
   - SRE compiles a post-incident SLA report within 48 hours: metrics, breach windows, and draft credit calculation.
   - Finance applies credits using the standard monthly invoice adjustment API: POST /billing/adjustments with payload {tenant_id, invoice_month, amount, reason}. (See billing API spec.)

Pricing and commercial levers
---------------------------
- Fidelity add-ons: priced as % uplift on base per-token rate. Example: silver +15%, gold +40%.
- Reserved Dedicated Pools: commit-based monthly pricing with performance SLAs; recommended for gold-tier customers.
- Overage and bursting: define a burst credit bucket (e.g., 10% of committed qps) billed at elevated per-token rate; sustained overage converts to a higher commit tier after 30 days.
- Credit cap: total monthly SLA credit exposure capped at 50% of monthly spend unless explicitly agreed.

Template contract language (plain-English snippets)
-------------------------------------------------
- Availability: "Provider will maintain availability of Covered Routes at or above [SLO%] measured monthly. If Provider fails to meet this SLO, Customer will be eligible for Service Credits as defined in the SLA credit schedule."
- Fidelity: "Provider will serve requests for Covered Routes using the agreed Fidelity Class. In the event Provider applies a downgrade that was not pre-authorized, Customer is eligible for Fidelity Breach Credits."
- Force Majeure / Planned Maintenance: "Planned maintenance windows of up to 4 hours/month are excluded from SLA calculations when communicated 48 hours in advance."

Rollout plan and timeline (90-day example)
-----------------------------------------
- Week 0–2: Discovery and benchmark prompt collection.
- Week 2–4: Onboard evaluation, sizing, and draft SLA offer.
- Week 4–6: Legal review and contract finalization.
- Week 6–8: Dedicated pool provisioning (if applicable) and pre-cutover canary.
- Week 8–12: Cutover, 30-day operating window with daily health syncs and 72-hour remediation SLA for initial breaches.

Operational metrics and dashboards (minimum set)
------------------------------------------------
- Per-tenant p50/p95/p99 latency over time (24h/7d/30d)
- Per-route token consumption and cost per 1000 tokens
- Fidelity-assignment events and downgrade counts
- Route-level availability and error budget consumption
- Incident-to-credit mapping dashboard

Implementation notes for private deployments
-------------------------------------------
- Private control plane must export the same telemetry schema as hosted: event_fidelity, latency_ms, tokens_in, tokens_out, region, model_variant.
- KMS policy checklist: ensure customer KMS keys are used for model artifacts and at-rest data when requested.
- On-prem packaging: coordinate with eng-private-deployments/day-2-ops for BASH install steps and VPN tunneling specifics.

Appendix A: Example monitoring PromQL snippets
-------------------------------------------
- p95 latency per tenant: histogram_quantile(0.95, sum(rate(request_latency_bucket[5m])) by (tenant, le))
- fidelity downgrade count: sum(increase(fidelity_downgrade_total[1h])) by (tenant)

Appendix B: Example billing adjustment payload (JSON)
---------------------------------------------------
- {
  "tenant_id": "tenant-123",
  "invoice_month": "2027-01",
  "amount": "-1500.00",
  "reason": "SLA credit for January p95 latency breach"
}

Ownership and RACI
------------------
- Product: finalize SLA catalog and fidelity definitions.
- Solutions Eng: collect workload data and run benchmarks.
- Eng-SRE: implement monitoring, runbooks, and enforcement hooks.
- Finance: implement crediting integration and monthly adjustments.
- Legal: approve clause templates and exceptions.
